findings.title: Data race on shared `err` and counter in parallel index build goroutines
findings.body: Inside `init`, each `group.Go` closure runs concurrently and does `totalBatchesIndexed++` (line 189) and `_, _, err = s.build(...)` (line 190). Both `totalBatchesIndexed` and the outer `err` are shared across goroutines, so this is a data race. A failing build can also overwrite another goroutine's error, so `group.Wait()`'s result may not reflect the real failure. The fix is to use a local `err` inside the closure and an atomic counter. This matters more now because the index is built synchronously in the constructor and the locking was made finer, so more builds run concurrently.

findings.title: TotalDocs iterates the cache map without holding cacheMu
findings.body: `TotalDocs` ranges over `b.cache` with no lock, while `BuildIndex` writes to the same map under `cacheMu.Lock()`. The commit removed the whole-function lock and only leaves the map write protected, so this read is now clearly unsynchronized. Concurrent `BuildIndex` calls (for example from `search.init` or a watch-triggered `getOrCreateIndex`) can cause a 'concurrent map read and map write' fatal error. `TotalDocs` should take `cacheMu.RLock()`.

findings.title: Finer locking lets concurrent builds for the same key race and overwrite each other
findings.body: Removing the function-wide lock means two `BuildIndex` calls for the same NamespacedResource can run at once. This can happen when `getOrCreateIndex` builds on a Search request while `search.init` is still building the same key, or when a watch event triggers a build. Both paths call `bleve.New` on the same directory for file-backed indexes, and the second call fails. For in-memory indexes, the second build silently replaces the cache entry, leaking the first index and any writes made to it. Nothing in `getOrCreateIndex` or `BuildIndex` deduplicates builds per key, and the TODO in `getOrCreateIndex` acknowledges this. A per-key singleflight or lock is needed before this change is safe.

findings.title: Index build failures now make NewResourceServer fail hard, changing startup behavior
findings.body: Init is now called synchronously from the constructor, so any error from `search.init` (for example `GetResourceStats` failing, or a bad index build) makes `NewResourceServer` return an error and the whole service fail to start. Previously these errors only surfaced as per-RPC errors and the service stayed up. The `once`/`initErr` mechanism also means the failure is never retried. The PR notes ask exactly this question about what depends on lazy initialization, and the description does not address the startup-failure behavior. Callers in module wiring and tests need to be checked, and the behavior change should be documented or tested.

findings.title: Events written during the index build are never indexed
findings.body: `init` lists resources and builds the index first, and only afterwards calls `WatchWriteEvents`. The SQL backend's poller starts from the latest resource version at the time `WatchWriteEvents` is called, so any write that lands between the `ListIterator` snapshot and that call is never replayed into the index. The index can therefore stay permanently stale for those objects. Now that the build runs at startup in the constructor and can take a long time, the window is larger. The watch should be started before the build, with events buffered and applied after the build.

findings.title: Context cancel function is leaked when startup Init fails
findings.body: `ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(...)` is created earlier in `NewResourceServer`. When `s.Init(ctx)` fails, the function returns `nil, err` without calling `s.cancel()`, and any goroutines started by the lifecycle hook or by `initWatcher`/`search.init` keep running with no owner. The error path should call `cancel()`.

findings.title: Unrelated postgres skip added to the storage server integration test
findings.body: The PR adds a skip for postgres in `TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer`. Nothing in the PR's stated changes (lazy init removal, tracing, locking) relates to postgres. The skip silently removes coverage for the storage-server startup path, which is the path this PR changes, and the TODO gives no tracking issue. Either the test should be fixed or the skip justified in the PR.
